R01R_A_DAYSQUIT_CIGS: DERIVED - Number of days since last smoked cigarettes

  Long Description: Recode of length of time since last smoked cigarette into days for
  respondents who have ever used AND (currently use not at all OR have used in the past
  30 days). Note: For all products, except cigarettes and hookah, former 30 day users
  includes some respondents who have indicated that while they have used in the past 30
  days, they have also used on zero of past 30 days. Respondents who are former 30 day
  users of cigarettes or hookah will not have reported using zero of the past 30 days.

  Algorithm:

  IF R01_AC1009_NN > 0 THEN { IF R01_AC1009_UN=1 THEN R01R_A_DAYSQUIT_CIGS
  = R01_AC1009_NN ELSE
  IF R01_AC1009_UN = 2 THEN R01R_A_DAYSQUIT_CIGS = R01_AC1009_NN*30.4375

R01_FORMER_USER_12MONTH_CIGS (Former users 12 Month): Has ever smoked a cigarette, has
smoked 100 cigarettes (lifetime), now does not smoke at all, and quit smoking within the past 12 months
(IF R01_AC1002 = 1 AND R01_AC1005 = 6 AND R01_AC1003 = 3 AND ((R01_AC1009_NN <= 365
AND R01_AC1009_UN = 1) OR (R01_AC1009_NN <= 12 AND R01_AC1009_UN = 2) OR
(R01_AC1009_NN = 1 AND R01_AC1009_UN = 3)), THEN R01_FORMER_USER_12MONTH_CIGS =
1 (YES).
ELSE, R01_FORMER_USER_12MONTH_CIGS = 2 (NO).). Note: might currently use other products.
R01_FORMER_USER_12MONTHPLUS_CIGS (Former users 12 Month Plus): Has ever smoked a
cigarette, has smoked 100 cigarettes (lifetime), now does not smoke at all, and quit smoking longer than
12 months ago (IF R01_AC1002 = 1 AND R01_AC1005 = 6 AND R01_AC1003 = 3 AND
((R01_AC1009_NN > 365 AND R01_AC1009_UN = 1) OR (R01_AC1009_NN > 12 AND
R01_AC1009_UN = 2) OR (R01_AC1009_NN > 1 AND R01_AC1009_UN = 3)), THEN
R01_FORMER_USER_12_MONTHPLUS_CIGS = 1 (YES).
ELSE, R01_FORMER_USER_12_MONTHPLUS_CIGS = 2 (NO).). Note: might currently use other
products.

If R01_FORMER_USER_12MONTH_CIGS = 1 OR R01_FORMER_USER_12MONTHPLUS_CIGS = 1,
go to R01_AC9002 and R01_AC9003.
If R01_CURRENT_USER_CIGS = 1, go to R01_AC9002 then BOX R01_AC2.
Else, if R01_AC1100 = 1, go to R01_AC9002.
Else, go to BOX R01_AC2.

Variable(s):        R02_AC1004
    In the past 30 days, have you smoked a cigarette, even one or two puffs?
                                 1     Yes                                       GO TO R02_AC1003
                                 2     No

    ASK: All adult respondents.

Variable(s):        R02_AC1002_12M
    In the past 12 months, have you smoked a cigarette, even one or two puffs?
                                 1     Yes
                                 2     No
                                -8     DON'T KNOW
                                -7     REFUSED
    ASK: Adult respondents who have not smoked a cigarette in the past 30 days or did not know or
    refused to report if they have smoked a cigarette in the past 30 days.
    ASK Specification: IF R02_AC1004 = 2, -8, -7.
    GOTO: Adult respondents who smoked a cigarette in the past 30 days or past 12 months, go to
    R02_AC1003.
    Else, adult respondents who did not smoke a cigarette in the past 12 months, who had ever smoked a
    cigarette and were not former established or former experimental cigarette smokers as of their last
    completed interview, go to R02_AC1009.
    Else, adult respondents who did not smoke a cigarette in the past 12 months, who had ever smoked a
    cigarette as of their last completed interview, go to R02_AC1010.
    Else, go to Box R02_ACV04.
    GOTO Specification: IF R02_AC1004 = 1 OR R02_AC1002_12M = 1, GO TO R02_AC1003.
    ELSE, IF R02_AC1002_12M = 2 AND (R01_EVER_USER_CIGS = 1 OR R01_YC1002 = 1) AND
    R01_FORMER_USER_CIGS != 1 AND R01_EXPERIMENTAL_FORMER_CIGS !=1, GO TO
    R02_AC1009.
    ELSE, IF R02_AC1002_12M = 2 AND (R01_EVER_USER_CIGS = 1 OR R01_YC1002 = 1), GO TO
    R02_AC1010.
    ELSE, GO TO BOX R02_ACV04.

  refused to report if they have smoked a cigarette in the past 30 days.

 BOX ID:             R03_ACR14
  Adult respondents who have smoked a cigarette in the past 30 days or in the past 12 months or adult
  respondents who have ever smoked a cigarette as of their last completed interview and did not know or
  refused to report if they smoked a cigarette in the past 12 months, go to R03_AC1003.
  Else, adult respondents who did not smoke a cigarette in the past 12 months and have ever smoked a
  cigarette as of their last completed interview and were not former experimental, new former established,
  or still former established cigarette smokers as of their last completed interview, go to R03_AC1009.
  Else, adult respondents who did not smoke a cigarette in the past 12 months, who had ever smoked a
  cigarette as of their last completed interview, go to R03_AC1010.
  Else, go to Box R03_ACV04.
  IF R03_AC1004 = 1 OR R03_AC1002_12M = 1 OR (R02_EVER_NEVER_CIGS = 1 AND
  R03_AC1002_12M = -8, -7), GO TO R03_AC1003.
  ELSE, IF R03_AC1002_12M = 2 AND R02_EVER_NEVER_CIGS = 1 AND R02_CIG_USER_STATUS
  ! = 3, 4, 5, GO TO R03_AC1009.
  ELSE, IF R03_AC1002_12M = 2 AND R02_EVER_NEVER_CIGS = 1, GO TO R03_AC1010.
  ELSE, GO TO BOX R03_ACV04.

  cohort adult respondents who have ever smoked a cigarette and have not smoked a cigarette in the

  Adult respondents who have smoked a cigarette in the past 30 days or in the past 12 months, or
  continuing and aged-up adult respondents who have ever smoked a cigarette as of their last completed
  interview and did not know or refused to report whether they have smoked a cigarette in the past 12
  months, or new cohort adult respondents who have ever smoked a cigarette and have not smoked a
  cigarette in the past 30 days or did not know or refused to report whether they have smoked a cigarette
  in the past 30 days and did not know or refused to report whether they have smoked a cigarette in the
  past 12 months, go to R04_AC1003.
  Else, continuing and aged-up adult respondents who have ever smoked a cigarette as of their last
  completed interview and were not former experimental, new former established, or still former
  established cigarette smokers as of their last completed interview and did not smoke a cigarette in the
  past 12 months, or new cohort adult respondents who have ever smoked a cigarette and have not
  smoked a cigarette in the past 30 days or did not know or refused to report whether they have smoked
  a cigarette in the past 30 days and did not smoke a cigarette in the past 12 months, go to
  R04_AC1009.
  Else, continuing and aged-up adult respondents who have ever smoked a cigarette as of their last
  completed interview and were not former experimental cigarette smokers as of their last completed
  interview and did not smoke a cigarette in the past 12 months, go to R04_AC1010.
  Else, go to Box R04_ACV04.

  R03_EVER_NEVER_CIGS = 1 AND R04_AC1002_12M = -8, -7) OR (R04_ADULTTYPE = 3 AND
  R04_AC1002_RS = 1 AND R04_AC1004 = 2, -8, -7 AND R04_AC1002_12M = -8, -7), GO TO
  R04_AC1003.
  ELSE, IF (R04_ADULTTYPE = 1, 2 AND R03_EVER_NEVER_CIGS = 1 AND
  R03_CIG_USER_STATUS != 3, 4, 5 AND R04_AC1002_12M = 2) OR (R04_ADULTTYPE = 3 AND
  R04_AC1002_RS = 1 AND R04_AC1004 = 2, -8, -7 AND R04_AC1002_12M = 2), GO TO
  R04_AC1009.
  ELSE, IF R04_ADULTTYPE = 1, 2 AND R03_EVER_NEVER_CIGS = 1 AND

1. Introduction
Westat prepared this report as a reference document for researchers using the Population
Assessment of Tobacco and Health (PATH) Study data. The PATH Study is a nationally
representative, longitudinal cohort study of adults and youth in the United States. This report
focuses on response rates and potential nonresponse biases for Wave 8, a data collection for youth
ages 12 to 17 and adults ages 18 or older, using select demographic, socioeconomic, and
tobacco-use measures.
Similar reports are also available for previous PATH Study data collections and can be found at the
following websites from the National Addiction & Health Data Archive Program (NAHDAP). The
reports for the primary waves (i.e., the waves that included all available sample youth and adults)
are located at the first website, and the reports for the special data collections, in which subgroups
of participants were surveyed, can be found at the second website.

•     Primary waves: Waves 1 to 4, 5, 6, and 7:
      https://www.icpsr.umich.edu/web/NAHDAP/studies/36231/datadocumentation
•     Special data collections: Waves 4.5, 5.5, 7.5, and the PATH Adult Telephone Study (PATH-ATS):
      https://www.icpsr.umich.edu/web/NAHDAP/studies/37519/datadocumentation
This document uses the term “participants” to refer to individuals who agreed to participate in the
PATH Study, regardless of whether they completed an interview at a particular wave. The term
“respondents” refers to the subset of participants who completed an interview or, in the case of
shadow youth (i.e., participants younger than age 12), verified their information with the study at a
particular wave. Where needed for clarity, this term may be qualified to indicate the type of
respondent (e.g., shadow youth respondent, adult interview respondent).
The PATH Study data support analyses of three cohorts: the Wave 1 Cohort, the Wave 4 Cohort, and
the Wave 7 Cohort (see Chapter 2). Wave 8 of the PATH Study (January 22, 2024, to December 31,
2024) was a primary wave of data collection for members of all three cohorts. This report
summarizes the Wave 8 nonresponse bias analyses conducted separately for the three PATH Study
cohorts. The analyses for the Wave 1 and Wave 4 Cohorts use an all-waves perspective rather than
a single-wave approach, which better serves the research community (see Section 3.2.1 for an
explanation). The analyses for the Wave 7 Cohort use a single-wave perspective and are similar to
those conducted for the Wave 4 Cohort at Wave 5. The potential for nonresponse bias in Wave 8
estimates based on the Wave 1 Cohort is evaluated conditioned on Wave 1 response, whereas the
Wave 4 Cohort is evaluated conditioned on Wave 4 response. Similarly, potential nonresponse bias
in estimates based on the Wave 7 Cohort is assessed conditioned on Wave 7 response. To
acknowledge potential nonresponse bias arising at the first wave of each cohort, brief summaries of
the findings from the Wave 1 nonresponse bias analyses, the Wave 4 nonresponse bias analyses for
the Wave 4 Cohort, and the Wave 7 nonresponse bias analyses for the Wave 7 Cohort are provided
in the following sections.

1.1        Wave 1 Cohort Nonresponse Bias Analyses at Wave 1

      characteristics of the respondents at Wave 1 aligned with estimates from the 2013 American
      Community Survey 1-year Public Use Microdata Sample (2013 ACS) when using the inverse
      probability of selection (IPS) weight for the PATH Study. Exceptions were found for single-
      person households, sex, education, and ethnicity when comparing Wave 1 estimates using the

2.1.5        Wave 6
Due to the Wave 5.5 and PATH-ATS special data collections in 2020, Wave 6 occurred
approximately 2 years after the start of the previous primary wave (Wave 5). In light of the
COVID-19 pandemic and for the continued safety of PATH Study participants and field interviewers,
Wave 6 data collection began with telephone interviewing. As conditions improved in certain parts
of the country and in compliance with local and state restrictions for COVID-19 mitigation,
in-person interviews began on May 7, 2021. In-person data collection was given priority; however,
each participant made the final decision regarding their preferred mode, and most of the Wave 6
interviews were conducted by telephone. No biospecimens were collected at Wave 6.

2.1.6        Wave 7
No special data collection occurred between primary Waves 6 and 7. The PATH Study sample was
replenished again at Wave 7, and a new cohort was formed. The main objectives of the Wave 7
sample design were to replenish the sample to account for attrition and participant aging. At the
start of Wave 7, the youngest participants in the Wave 4 Cohort were almost all age 15 or older, so
the replenishment effort provided a means of selecting a new sample of youth ages 12 to 14, in
addition to a new shadow sample of youth ages 9 to 11 to be interviewed after they reach age 12 at
later waves. The replenishment also provided the opportunity for a second panel conditioning
assessment. Active-duty members of the military at the time of replenishment were ineligible, as
were all persons living in institutional and noninstitutional group quarters other than college
dormitories.
A probability replenishment sample of adults, youth, and shadow youth (ages 9 to 11) was selected
from the CNP at Wave 7, including persons who were not in the CNP at the time of Wave 4 (e.g.,
recent immigrants, those returning from the military). Only members of the Wave 4 Cohort who
responded, were at least age 15, and were in the CNP at the time of Wave 7 were combined with the
Wave 7 replenishment sample to form the new Wave 7 Cohort. As a result, the target population for
the Wave 7 Cohort was the CNP who were ages 9 or older at the time of Wave 7.
As part of the Wave 7 replenishment effort, adults, youth, and shadow youth were sampled within
the existing PATH Study sample segments from among the addresses not selected for Wave 1 or
Wave 4. The Wave 7 within-household sampling procedures were similar to those used at Waves 1
and 4, with sampling rates varying for adults by age, race, and tobacco-use status. 6 The
within-household sampling rates were designed to increase the Wave 7 adult and youth sample
sizes to a level commensurate with Wave 4 sample sizes. This approach required consideration for
the expected combined effect of the aging of continuing sample participants and the loss of sample
size due to attrition by the time of Wave 7. The number of responding adults from the continuing
sample at Wave 7 was projected to be close to Wave 4 levels without replenishment. However,
small samples of adults were selected from each of the sampling domains to allow representation of
immigrants and other adults who had joined the CNP since Wave 4, and to support a panel
conditioning assessment to monitor the potential effects of participating in the PATH Study over
time. The targeted adult sample sizes made it feasible to sample adults at Phase 1 based only on age
and race (as reported by the household screener respondent) and to subsample at Phase 2 based on
self-reported tobacco use, in addition to self-reported age and race.


6   The main difference between the definition of tobacco use for sampling adults at Waves 1, 4, and 7 is that “e-cigarettes”
    were replaced by “electronic nicotine products” starting at Wave 4, and ever use of IQOS, nicotine pouches, and other
    types of oral nicotine products were added at Wave 7.
